description: Sample scenarios. Each entry is sent byte-for-byte by the local sender and decoded at receive time. Entries with the same raw_hex are the same bytes interpreted by different databases.

scenarios.title: VehicleStatus - nominal
scenarios.note: Motorola 12-bit torque, signed coolant with offset, text enum.

scenarios.title: VehicleStatus - negative boundary
scenarios.note: Torque at the most negative value its 12 signed bits can carry (-1024 raw = -512 Nm), coolant at -40 degC.

scenarios.title: VehicleStatus - declared range exceeded
scenarios.note: Torque 1010 Nm is encodable (raw 2020 fits 12 signed bits) but above the declared maximum 1000. The receiver must flag the declared-range violation while keeping the frame; the frame itself is valid.

scenarios.title: BodyCommand - Mode=1 Drive
scenarios.note: Mode=1 selects MotorRpm and MotorCurrent. The Charge* and ServiceCode bits belong to other branches.

scenarios.title: BodyCommand - Mode=2 Charge
scenarios.note: Mode=2 selects ChargeVoltage and ChargeTimer; the Drive-only signals must read as not applicable even though their bits contain data.

scenarios.title: BodyCommand - Mode=5 (no branch defined)
scenarios.note: No m5 branch exists. Every multiplexed signal must be not applicable, never zero. The bytes still carry 0x11 0x22 ... so a zero would be visibly wrong.

scenarios.title: DiagNested - Group=1 Sub=2 selects LeafA
scenarios.note: Nested multiplexing: Group=1 exposes Sub, Sub=2 selects LeafA. LeafB is not applicable.

scenarios.title: DiagNested - Group=5 blocks Sub
scenarios.note: Group=5 means the Sub selector itself is not applicable, so everything below it is unknown. A decoder that walks the tree unconditionally would invent values here.

scenarios.title: ChargerStatus - 29-bit extended, Motorola
scenarios.note: Extended id 0x18FF50E5. Both 16-bit values are Motorola with the start bit as MSB and the second one is signed.

scenarios.title: VehicleStatus - 6-byte frame
scenarios.note: The definition expects 8 bytes, the sender emits 6. LampState (bits 60..63) leaves the frame: it must be reported as unreadable, while the signals that fit still decode.

scenarios.title: VehicleStatus - 10-byte frame
scenarios.note: Longer than the definition. CANLab keeps the extra bytes in the raw view and flags the length; it does not truncate the trace.

scenarios.title: FreeCounter - decoded by a database that does not define it
scenarios.note: 0x103 exists only in demo_ecu.dbc. Sent while reading through conflict_a.dbc, it must show 'no such message' plus the raw bytes, not a fake decode.

scenarios.title: Powertrain - the same bytes under conflict_a and conflict_b
scenarios.note: Sent to both databases. A reads Torque as 12-bit Intel signed; B reads a 16-bit Motorola field at the same offset, and B also declares 6 bytes. The comparison panel explains the difference field by field.

scenarios.title: Thermal - Mode=2 selects PumpRpm in A, PumpPressure in B
scenarios.note: Both files define the same bits for Mode=2 but call them different things with different units and scales. This is the 'is the definition wrong or the frame wrong' case.

scenarios.title: ConflictOverlap - overlap in A, out-of-frame tail in both
scenarios.note: A overlaps PackVoltage and TorqueRaw on bits 12..15 and both files' SigOverrun reaches past byte 7. The definition findings locate each fault by source line; the frame itself is still displayed.
